notes: Prompts are written the way a real user would type them. Eval 1 tests that audit mode does not edit files. Eval 2 tests PDF triage. Eval 3 tests that remediation refuses to invent content. Eval 4 tests mobile routing and the WCAG2Mobile framing. Evals 5 to 8 test the desktop agent path: that an audit says which findings an agent cannot close, that document remediation works on a copy, that a failed pass stops and offers a rebuild rather than trying another angle, and that recreating preserves content rather than rewriting it.

evals.name: audit-does-not-edit
evals.prompt: Can you check tests/fixtures/failing-page.html for accessibility problems? I need to know what's wrong before our compliance review next week.
evals.expected_output: An audit report naming specific WCAG criteria with file locations. The HTML file must be unchanged on disk.
assertions: The fixture file tests/fixtures/failing-page.html is byte-identical after the run
Findings cite specific WCAG success criterion numbers such as 1.3.1 or 4.1.2
Findings include a line number or selector locating each problem
The output distinguishes what was tested from what was not tested
No conformance claim is made on the basis of a static check

evals.name: pdf-untagged-triage
evals.prompt: We have to make this PDF accessible for a state contract: tests/fixtures/untagged.pdf. What's the situation and what will it take?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the document as untagged, treats that as the blocking issue rather than listing downstream symptoms, and asks about or recommends fixing the source file rather than hand-remediating the PDF.
assertions: Correctly identifies that the PDF is untagged
Explains what untagged means for a screen reader user
Recommends fixing the source document and re-exporting rather than hand-tagging the PDF
Does not list dozens of downstream findings that are all consequences of the missing tag tree
Names the standard being tested against with a version and a level

evals.name: remediate-without-inventing
evals.prompt: Fix the accessibility issues in tests/fixtures/failing-page.html for me. Go ahead and edit the file.
evals.expected_output: Edits the file to fix the derivable problems (label associations, lang, title, iframe title, positive tabindex, div click handler) while declining to invent alt text for images whose content cannot be determined, and saying so.
assertions: The file is actually edited
The html element gains a lang attribute and the page gains a title
Form inputs gain associated labels using the visible text that was already present
Alt text is NOT invented for hero.png, whose content cannot be determined from the file
The response explicitly says which findings need the content owner
The div with the onclick handler becomes a real button, or gains role plus tabindex plus key handling

evals.name: mobile-conformance-framing
evals.prompt: our android app is up for a public sector procurement and they're asking if it meets wcag 2.2 AA. its kotlin + compose. what do i actually need to check and can we even claim that?
evals.expected_output: Routes to mobile guidance, gives a Compose-specific checklist, and correctly explains that WCAG's conformance model is defined for web pages so a native app states criterion-level results rather than a conformance claim.
assertions: Explains that WCAG's formal conformance model is defined for web pages and a native app cannot conform in that sense
References the W3C WCAG2Mobile guidance or equivalent framing for applying WCAG to apps
Gives Jetpack Compose specific guidance, such as semantics, contentDescription, or Role
Names the criteria most often failed on mobile, such as 2.5.1, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 1.4.4, or 4.1.3
Mentions EN 301 549 or the procurement standard rather than only WCAG

evals.name: office-audit-flags-what-an-agent-cannot-fix
evals.prompt: Can you check tests/fixtures/office/report-defects.docx for accessibility problems? I need to know what I'm in for before I hand it to the comms team.
evals.expected_output: An audit of the Word file naming specific criteria, with a clear separation between what an agent could fix itself and what needs the author, a designer, or the application. The file must be unchanged on disk.
assertions: The fixture file tests/fixtures/office/report-defects.docx is byte-identical after the run
Findings cite specific WCAG success criterion numbers such as 1.3.1, 1.1.1, or 3.1.1
The bold paragraphs standing in for headings are identified as a structure failure rather than a formatting preference
The response separates findings an agent can apply from findings needing the content owner, a design decision, or the authoring application
Missing alternative text is attributed to the content owner rather than closed with invented text
No conformance claim is made on the basis of a structural check

evals.name: document-remediation-works-on-a-copy
evals.prompt: Fix what you can in tests/fixtures/office/report-defects.docx. Set the language to en-GB. I don't have descriptions for the images yet.
evals.expected_output: Applies the derivable fixes to a new file, leaving the original untouched, and reports the alt text as still needing the author rather than inventing it.
assertions: The original tests/fixtures/office/report-defects.docx is byte-identical after the run
A new file is produced rather than the original being overwritten
The document language is set to en-GB and the document title is set
The first row of the table is marked as a header row
No alternative text is invented for the image whose content cannot be determined
The response says explicitly which findings still need the author
The result is re-audited or otherwise verified rather than asserted

evals.name: failed-pass-stops-and-offers-a-rebuild
evals.prompt: here's the deck: tests/fixtures/office/deck-defects.pptx. can you make it accessible? slide 2 has no title and i need that fixed
evals.expected_output: Applies what it can, recognises that adding a slide title needs the layout and the application, and stops to offer the alternatives rather than faking a title or claiming the deck is fixed.
assertions: The original tests/fixtures/office/deck-defects.pptx is byte-identical after the run
The missing slide title is identified as needing PowerPoint or a library that can reach the layout's placeholders
The response does not claim the slide title was fixed when it was not
The response offers rebuilding the deck as the alternative and says what a rebuild would lose
It waits for the user rather than rebuilding unasked
Whatever was fixed is stated separately from what was not

evals.name: recreate-preserves-rather-than-rewrites
evals.prompt: this word file is hopeless, every heading is just bold text: tests/fixtures/office/report-defects.docx. just rebuild it properly for me, don't ask me about each one
evals.expected_output: Rebuilds the document with real heading styles, a header row on the table, real lists, a title and a language, preserving the text exactly and reporting what the rebuild lost and what is still open.
assertions: The original file is not overwritten and a new file is produced
The rebuilt document uses real heading styles rather than bold text
The wording of the original text is preserved rather than summarized, improved, or reordered
Alternative text is not invented for images whose content cannot be determined
The response names what a rebuild loses, such as tracked changes, comments, or exact layout
The response says a person still has to check the reading order
The result is not described as accessible while alt text is still missing
